Abdullah ibn Ali narrated that some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were sitting one day, and a Jew was near them. Some of them said: "I come to my wife while she lies on her side." Another said: "I come to her while she is standing." Another said: "I come to her while she is on her side." Another said: "I come to her while she is kneeling." The Jew said: "You are nothing but like animals. But we only have intercourse with her in one position." So Allah revealed this verse. This is the view of Ikrimah.

The second: meaning from whatever direction you wish, toward her front passage, or from her back toward her front passage.

Jabir narrated that the Jews said: "The Arabs have intercourse with women from behind, and when they do so the child is born cross-eyed." So Allah refuted their claim and said: ﴿Your women are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth as you wish﴾. This is the view of Ibn Abbas and al-Rabi'.

The third: meaning from wherever you wish. This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and others.

The fourth: how you wish, whether you practice coitus interruptus (al-'azl) or not. This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib.

The fifth: wherever you wish, from the front or from the back. This was transmitted by Nafi' from Ibn Umar, and he reported it from others too. (p-285)

Hubaysh ibn Abdullah al-San'ani narrated from Ibn Abbas that some people from Himyar came to the Prophet ﷺ asking him about various matters. A man among them said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am a man who loves women. What is your view on this?" So Allah revealed in Surah al-Baqarah the explanation of what they had asked about. He revealed concerning what the man asked: ﴿Your women are a tilth for you, so come to your tilth as you wish﴾. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Facing or with her back to you, as long as it is in the vagina."

﴿And send forth for yourselves﴾, meaning good deeds. This is the view of al-Suddi.

The second: "send forth for yourselves" the remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, during intercourse. This is the view of Ibn Abbas.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 2, verse 224–225:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not make Allah an obstacle (ʿurḍah) in your oaths﴾. As for ʿurḍah in the speech of the Arabs, it means strength and vehemence. There are two interpretations of it here:

The first: that you swear by Allah, exalted is He, in every matter, true or false, thereby cheapening His name and making it an obstacle.

The second: that the meaning of ʿurḍah is a pretext (ʿillah) by which one makes excuses regarding his piety. Concerning this there are two aspects. The first: that one refrains from doing good and from reconciling between people when asked, saying: "An oath is upon me that I will not do that," or he swears by Allah immediately and then makes the oath an excuse for abandoning good. This is the view of Ṭāwūs, Qatādah, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr.

The second: that one swears by Allah that he will do good and righteousness, but in his action he intends the righteousness of his oath, not the desire to do it.

Regarding His saying: ﴿that you be righteous (an tabarrū)﴾, there are two views: The first: that you be righteous in your oaths. The second: that you be righteous toward your relatives (arḥām).

﴿And that you be mindful of Allah and make peace between people﴾ is the well-known reconciliation. ﴿And Allah is Hearing, Knowing﴾: Hearing of your oaths, Knowing of your beliefs.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional (al-laghw) in your oaths﴾. As for al-laghw in the speech of the Arabs, it is every speech that is blameworthy and superfluous, having no meaning. It is derived from their saying: "So-and-so committed laghw in his speech" when he said something ugly. From this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when they hear idle talk, they turn away from it﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 55]. As for the laghw of oaths for which Allah, exalted is He, does not hold one accountable, there are seven interpretations:

The first: what the tongue utters without intention, such as saying: "No, by Allah," and "Yes, by Allah." This is the view of ʿĀʾishah and Ibn ʿAbbās, and al-Shāfiʿī adopted it. ʿAbd Allah ibn Maymūn related from ʿAwf al-Aʿrābī, from al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Ḥasan, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a people shooting arrows (yanḍilūn, meaning they were shooting), and with the Prophet ﷺ was a man from his companions. A man from the people shot, and said: 'By Allah, he hit it! By Allah, I missed!' The one who was with the Prophet ﷺ said: 'The man has broken his oath, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: '(Nay, the oaths of archers are laghw, and there is no expiation nor punishment.)'"

The second: that the laghw of an oath is that one swears regarding a matter, thinking that it is as he swore, then it becomes clear that it is contrary to that. This is the view of Abū Hurayrah.

The third: that the laghw of an oath is that its swearer swears by it in a state of anger, without resolve or determination of the heart, but merely as a filler of speech. This is the view of Ṭāwūs.

Yaḥyā ibn Abī Kathīr related from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "(There is no oath in anger)."

The fourth: that the laghw of an oath is that one swears by it in disobedience, so there is no expiation for it. This is the view of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Masrūq, and al-Shaʿbī. ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb related from his father, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "(Whoever vows concerning what he does not possess, there is no vow for him; whoever swears to an act of disobedience, there is no oath for him; and whoever swears to sever the ties of kinship, there is no oath for him.)"

The fifth: that the laghw in an oath is when the swearer invokes a curse upon himself, such as saying: "If I do not do such-and-such, may Allah blind my sight, or diminish my wealth, or I am a disbeliever in Allah." This is the view of Zayd ibn Aslam.

The sixth: that the laghw of an oath is that in which the swearer breaks his oath forgetfully. This is the view of al-Nakhaʿī.

Then His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned﴾. Concerning this there are three interpretations: The first: that one swears falsely or upon falsehood. This is the view of Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī.

The second: that one swears deliberately. This is the view of Mujāhid.

The third: that it is the belief in associating partners with Allah and disbelief. This is the view of Ibn Zayd.

﴿And Allah is Forgiving, Forbearing﴾: Forgiving toward His servants regarding the idle oaths they utter, Forbearing in not requiting with punishment for their sins those who do good.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 2, verses 226–227:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿For those who swear off their wives, a waiting period of four months.﴾ The meaning of His saying ﴿yu'lūna﴾ is: they swear (yuqsimūna). The "ilyah" (إلية) is the oath (al-yamin). The poet said:

"We were spared the harshness of Nizar, and we took them as oath-takers before him."

In the speech there is an ellipsis; its estimated form is: "For those who swear off (an oath) that they will abstain from their wives," but the (ellipsis) is indicated only by the apparent sense of the speech.

They differed concerning the oath by which one becomes a muli (one who has sworn off, mu'li, from ila', the vow of abstinence), on two opinions. One: it is the oath by Allah alone. The second: it is any oath whose violation obliges the expiation (kaffarah), provided it was not already obligatory for him. Both opinions are attributed to al-Shafi'i.

They differed concerning the one who, when he swears about something, becomes a muli, on three statements. The first: it is that he swears about his wife, in a state of anger, in a manner intended to harm her, that he will not have intercourse with her in her private part. As for one who swears not in a manner intended to harm and not in anger, he is not a muli. This is the view of 'Ali, Ibn 'Abbas and 'Ata'.

The second: it is that he swears he will not have intercourse with her in her private part, whether in anger or not in anger. This is the view of al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, al-Nakha'i and al-Shafi'i.

The third: it is any oath he swears with the intention of distressing his wife, regarding intercourse or otherwise, such as his saying: "By Allah, I will surely distress you or I will surely enrage you." This is the view of Ibn al-Musayyib, al-Sha'bi and al-Hakam.

Then He said, may He be exalted: ﴿And if they return﴾, meaning they come back. The fay' (فيء) and the return (ruju') are a movement from one state to another, as in His saying: ﴿until it returns to the command of Allah﴾ [al-Hujurat: 9], that is, until it returns. From it is the saying of the poet:

"So she returned without fulfilling what she had come for, and among human needs is that which is not fulfilled."

(p-289)

There are three interpretations of fay'. The first: it is intercourse only and nothing else. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, and of those who say that the muli is the one who swears about intercourse specifically and not other things.

The second: it is intercourse by one who is not excused, with the intention in the heart. This is the view of al-Hasan and 'Ikrimah.

The third: it is returning by the tongue, with every indication that it is contentment. This was said by Ibn Mas'ud, and by those who say that the muli is the one who swears to distress his wife.

Then He said, may He be exalted: ﴿then indeed Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾. In this there are three interpretations. The first: He intends the forgiveness of the sin, and upon it is the expiation. This was said by 'Ali, Ibn 'Abbas and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib.

The second: Forgiving by lightening the expiation and dropping it. This is the view of those who claim that expiation is not obligatory where the breaking of the oath was righteous. This was said by al-Hasan and Ibrahim.

The third: Forgiving of the sinfulness of the oath, Merciful in granting the permission of an exit from it through expiation. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

Then He said, may He be exalted: ﴿And if they resolve upon divorce﴾, the verse.

Ibn 'Abbas recited: (وإن عزموا السراح) (wa-in 'azamu al-sarah), and in this there are three interpretations. The first: the resolve of one who does not return until four months pass, whereupon she is divorced by that.

Those who held this differed concerning the divorce that befalls her, on two opinions. One: it is an irrevocable single divorce (talaqah ba'inah). This is the view of 'Uthman, 'Ali, Ibn Zayd, Zayd ibn Thabit, Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Umar and Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: it is a revocable single divorce (talaqah raj'iyyah). This is the view of Ibn al-Musayyib, Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, and Ibn Shubrumah.

The second interpretation: when the four months pass, he is obliged to either return or divorce. This is the view of 'Umar, 'Ali in the narration of 'Amr ibn Salamah, and Ibn Abi Layla from him, 'Uthman in the narration of Tawus from him, Abu al-Darda', 'A'ishah, and Ibn 'Umar in the narration of Nafi' from him.

Suhayl ibn Abi Salih narrated from his father, who said: "I asked twelve men from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ about the man who swears off from his wife, and all of them said: 'Nothing is incumbent upon him until four months pass, whereupon he is made to stand (before the judge); if he returns, well and good, and otherwise he divorces.'" This is the view of al-Shafi'i and the people of Madinah.

The third: the ila' is nothing (has no effect). This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, in the narration of 'Amr ibn Dinar from him.

Regarding His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿then indeed Allah is Hearing, Knowing﴾, there are two interpretations. The first: He hears his ila'. The second: He hears his divorce.

Regarding ("'Alim", Knowing), there are two interpretations. The first: He knows his intention. The second: He knows his patience.

قَوْلُهُ عَزَّ وجَلَّ: ﴿والمُطَلَّقاتُ يَتَرَبَّصْنَ بِأنْفُسِهِنَّ ثَلاثَةَ قُرُوءٍ﴾ يَعْنِي المُخَلَّياتِ، والطَّلاقُ: التَّخْلِيَةُ كَما يُقالُ لِلنَّعْجَةِ المُهْمَلَةِ بِغَيْرِ راعٍ: طالِقٌ، فَسُمِّيَتِ المَرْأةُ المُخَلّى سَبِيلُها بِما سُمِّيَتْ بِهِ النَّعْجَةُ المُهْمَلُ أمْرُها، وقِيلَ: إنَّهُ مَأْخُوذٌ مِن طَلْقِ الفَرَسِ، وهو ذَهابُهُ شَوْطًا لا يُمْنَعُ، فَسُمِّيَتِ المَرْأةُ المُخَلّاةُ طالِقًا لِأنَّها لا تَمْنَعُ مِن نَفْسِها بَعْدَ أنْ كانَتْ مَمْنُوعَةً، ولِذَلِكَ قِيلَ لِذاتِ الزَّوْجِ: إنَّها في حِبالِهِ لِأنَّها كالمَعْقُولَةِ بِشَيْءٍ، وأمّا قَوْلُهُمْ: طَلَقَتِ المَرْأةُ فَمَعْناهُ غَيْرُ هَذا، إنَّما يُقالُ: طَلَقَتِ المَرْأةُ إذا نَفَسَتْ، هَذا مِنَ الطَّلْقِ وهو وجَعُ الوِلادَةِ، والأوَّلُ مِنَ الطَّلاقِ.

ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿يَتَرَبَّصْنَ بِأنْفُسِهِنَّ ثَلاثَةَ قُرُوءٍ﴾ أيْ مُدَّةَ ثَلاثَةِ قُرُوءٍ، واخْتَلَفُوا في الأقْراءِ عَلى قَوْلَيْنِ: أحَدُهُما: هي الحِيَضُ، وهو قَوْلُ عُمَرَ، وعَلِيٍّ، وابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، وأبِي (p-٢٩١) مُوسى، ومُجاهِدٍ، وقَتادَةَ، والضَّحّاكِ، وعِكْرِمَةَ، والسُّدِّيِّ، ومالِكٍ، وأبِي حَنِيفَةَ، وأهْلِ العِراقِ، اسْتِشْهادًا بِقَوْلِ الشّاعِرِ:

يا رُبَّ ذِي صِغْنٍ عَلَيَّ فارِضٍ ∗∗∗ لَهُ قُرُوءٌ كَقُرُوءِ الحائِضِ

(O many a one harboring rancor against me, a hostile one, who has periods like the periods of a menstruating woman.)

والثّانِي: هي الأطْهارُ، وهو قَوْلُ عائِشَةَ، وابْنِ عُمَرَ، وزَيْدِ بْنِ ثابِتٍ، والزُّهْرِيِّ، وأبانَ بْنِ عُثْمانَ، والشّافِعِيِّ، وأهْلِ الحِجازِ، اسْتِشْهادًا بِقَوْلِ الأعْشى:

أفِي كُلِّ عامٍ أنْتَ جاشِمٌ غَزْوَةً ∗∗∗ تَشُدُّ لِأقْصاها عَزِيمَ عَزائِكا
مُوَرِّثَةً مالًا وفي الحَيِّ رِفْعَةٌ ∗∗∗ لِما ضاعَ فِيها مِن قُرُوءِ نِسائِكا

(Is it every year that you undertake a raid, its farthest reach tightened by the resolve of your endurance, / leaving wealth behind and honor among the tribe, for what was lost in it of your women's qurū'?)

واخْتَلَفُوا في اشْتِقاقِ القُرْءِ عَلى قَوْلَيْنِ: أحَدُهُما: أنَّ القُرْءَ الِاجْتِماعُ، ومِنهُ أُخِذَ اسْمُ القُرْآنِ لِاجْتِماعِ حُرُوفِهِ، وقِيلَ: قَدْ قَرَأ الطَّعامَ في شِدْقِهِ وقَرَأ الماءَ في حَوْضِهِ إذا جَمَعَهُ، وقِيلَ: ما قَرَأتِ النّاقَةُ سَلًى قَطُّ، أيْ لَمْ يَجْتَمِعْ رَحِمُها عَلى ولَدٍ قَطُّ، قالَ عَمْرُو بْنُ كُلْثُومٍ:

تُرِيكَ إذا دَخَلَتْ عَلى خَلاءٍ ∗∗∗ وقَدْ أمِنَتْ عُيُونَ الكاشِحِينا
ذِراعَيْ عَيْطَلٍ أدْماءَ بِكْرٍ ∗∗∗ هَجانَ اللَّوْنِ لَمْ تَقْرَأْ جَنِينا

(She shows you, when she enters a secluded place, safe from the eyes of the malicious, / the two forearms of a tall, white, virgin she-camel of pure, mixed color, who has not gathered a fetus in her womb.)

وَهَذا قَوْلُ الأصْمَعِيِّ، والأخْفَشِ، والكِسائِيِّ، والشّافِعِيِّ، فَمَن جَعَلَ القُرُوءَ اسْمًا لِلْحَيْضِ سَمّاهُ بِذَلِكَ، لِاجْتِماعِ الدَّمِ في الرَّحِمِ، ومَن جَعَلَهُ اسْمًا لِلطُّهْرِ فَلِاجْتِماعِهِ في البَدَنِ.

والقَوْلُ الثّانِي: أنَّ القُرْءَ الوَقْتُ، لِمَجِيءِ الشَّيْءِ المُعْتادِ مَجِيؤُهُ لِوَقْتٍ مَعْلُومٍ، ولِإدْبارِ الشَّيْءِ المُعْتادِ إدْبارُهُ لِوَقْتٍ مَعْلُومٍ، وكَذَلِكَ قالَتِ العَرَبُ: أقْرَأْتُ حاجَةَ فُلانٍ عِنْدِي، أيْ دَنا وقْتُها وحانَ قَضاؤُها.

وَأقْرَأ النَّجْمُ إذا جاءَ وقْتُ أُفُولِهِ، وقَرَأ إذا جاءَ وقْتُ طُلُوعِهِ، قالَ الشّاعِرُ:

إذا ما الثُّرَيّا وقَدْ أقْرَأتْ ∗∗∗ ... ... ...

(p-٢٩٢)

وَقِيلَ: أقْرَأتِ الرِّيحُ، إذا هَبَّتْ لِوَقْتِها، قالَ الهُذَلِيُّ:

كَرِهْتُ العَقْرَ عَقْرَ بَنِي شَلِيلٍ ∗∗∗ إذا لِقارِئِها الرِّياحُ

يَعْنِي هَبَّتْ لِوَقْتِها، وهَذا قَوْلُ أبِي عَمْرِو بْنِ العَلاءِ.

فَمَن جَعَلَ القُرْءَ اسْمًا لِلْحَيْضِ، فَلِأنَّهُ وقْتُ خُرُوجِ الدَّمِ المُعْتادِ، ومَن جَعَلَهُ اسْمًا لِلطُّهْرِ، فَلِأنَّهُ وقْتُ احْتِباسِ الدَّمِ المُعْتادِ.

ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿وَلا يَحِلُّ لَهُنَّ أنْ يَكْتُمْنَ ما خَلَقَ اللَّهُ في أرْحامِهِنَّ﴾ فِيهِ ثَلاثَةُ تَأْوِيلاتٍ: أحَدُها: أنَّهُ الحَيْضُ، وهو قَوْلُ عِكْرِمَةَ، والزُّهْرِيِّ، والنَّخَعِيِّ.

والثّانِي: أنَّهُ الحَمْلُ، قالَهُ عُمَرُ وابْنُ عَبّاسٍ.

والثّالِثُ: أنَّهُ الحَمْلُ والحَيْضُ قالَهُ عُمَرُ ومُجاهِدٌ.

﴿إنْ كُنَّ يُؤْمِنَّ بِاللَّهِ واليَوْمِ الآخِرِ﴾ وعِيدٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ لَهُنَّ، واخْتُلِفَ في سَبَبِ الوَعِيدِ عَلى قَوْلَيْنِ: أحَدُهُما: لِما يَسْتَحِقُّهُ الزَّوْجُ مِنَ الرَّجْعَةِ، وهو قَوْلُ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ.

والثّانِي: لِإلْحاقِ نَسَبِ الوَلِيدِ بِغَيْرِهِ كَفِعْلِ الجاهِلِيَّةِ، وهو قَوْلُ قَتادَةَ.

ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿وَبُعُولَتُهُنَّ أحَقُّ بِرَدِّهِنَّ في ذَلِكَ﴾ البَعْلُ: الزَّوْجُ، سُمِّيَ بِذَلِكَ، لِعُلُوِّهِ عَلى الزَّوْجَةِ بِما قَدْ مَلَكَهُ عَنْ زَوْجِيَّتِها ومِنهُ قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿أتَدْعُونَ بَعْلا﴾ [الصّافّاتِ: ١٢٥] أيْ رَبًّا لِعُلُوِّهِ بِالرُّبُوبِيَّةِ، ﴿أحَقُّ بِرَدِّهِنَّ في ذَلِكَ﴾ أيْ بِرَجْعَتِهِنَّ، وهَذا مَخْصُوصٌ في الطَّلاقِ الرَّجْعِيِّ (the revocable divorce) دُونَ البائِنِ.

﴿إنْ أرادُوا إصْلاحًا﴾ يَعْنِي إصْلاحَ ما بَيْنَهُما مِنَ الطَّلاقِ.

ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿وَلَهُنَّ مِثْلُ الَّذِي عَلَيْهِنَّ بِالمَعْرُوفِ﴾ وفِيهِ ثَلاثَةُ تَأْوِيلاتٍ: أحَدُها: ولَهُنَّ مِن حُسْنِ الصُّحْبَةِ والعِشْرَةِ بِالمَعْرُوفِ عَلى أزْواجِهِنَّ، مِثْلُ الَّذِي عَلَيْهِنَّ مِنَ الطّاعَةِ، فِيما أوْجَبَهُ اللَّهُ تَعالى عَلَيْهِنَّ لِأزْواجِهِنَّ، وهو قَوْلُ الضَّحّاكِ. (p-٢٩٣)

والثّانِي: ولَهُنَّ عَلى أزْواجِهِنَّ مِنَ التَّصَنُّعِ والتَّزَيُّنِ، مِثْلُ ما لِأزْواجِهِنَّ، وهو قَوْلُ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ.

والثّالِثُ: أنَّ الَّذِي لَهُنَّ عَلى أزْواجِهِنَّ، تَرْكُ مُضارَّتِهِنَّ، كَما كانَ ذَلِكَ لِأزْواجِهِنَّ، وهو قَوْلُ أبِي جَعْفَرٍ.

ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿وَلِلرِّجالِ عَلَيْهِنَّ دَرَجَةٌ﴾ وفِيهِ خَمْسَةُ تَأْوِيلاتٍ: أحَدُها: فَضْلُ المِيراثِ والجِهادِ، وهو قَوْلُ مُجاهِدٍ.

والثّانِي: أنَّهُ الإمْرَةُ والطّاعَةُ، وهو قَوْلُ زَيْدِ بْنِ أسْلَمَ، وابْنِهِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ.

والثّالِثُ: أنَّهُ إعْطاءُ الصَّداقِ، وأنَّهُ إذا قَذَفَها لاعَنَها، وإنْ قَذَفَتْهُ حُدَّتْ، وهو قَوْلُ الشَّعْبِيِّ.

والرّابِعُ: أفْضالُهُ عَلَيْها، وأداءُ حَقِّها إلَيْها، والصَّفْحُ عَمّا يَجِبُ لَهُ مِنَ الحُقُوقِ عَلَيْها، وهو قَوْلُ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ وقَتادَةَ.

والخامِسُ: أنْ جُعِلَ لَهُ لِحْيَةٌ، وهو قَوْلُ حُمَيْدٍ.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Divorce is twice﴾. There are two interpretations of this.

The first: it is an explanation of the number of divorces, and its meaning is: with three. The husband may take back his wife after the first two, but may not take her back after the third. This is the view of 'Urwah and Qatadah. Hisham ibn 'Urwah narrated from his father, who said: "A man used to divorce his wife while forgetful. If he took her back shortly before her 'iddah (waiting period) ended, she would remain his wife. A man from the Ansar became angry with his wife and said to her, 'I will not approach you, and you will not be free from me.' She said to him, 'How? I will divorce you, and when your term draws near I will take you back.' So she complained of her husband to the Prophet (ﷺ), and Allah, may He be exalted, revealed: ﴿Divorce is twice﴾, the verse."

The second interpretation: it is an explanation of the sunnah (prescribed way) of divorce, that one pronounces a single divorce at each occasion. This is the view of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then retain her in kindness or release her with good treatment﴾. There are two interpretations of this.

The first: this refers to the third divorce. Sufyan narrated from Isma'il ibn Sumay', from Abu Razin, who said: "A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said, 'Divorce is twice, so where is the third?' He (ﷺ) said: ﴿Then retain her in kindness or release her with good treatment﴾." This is the view of 'Ata' and Mujahid.

The second: ﴿Then retain her in kindness﴾ refers to taking her back after the second divorce, and ﴿or release her with good treatment﴾ refers to refraining from taking her back until the 'iddah ends. This is the view of al-Suddi and al-Dahhak.

Ihsan (good treatment) is to fulfil her rights and to refrain from harming her.

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿It is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them﴾, meaning from the dower (sadaq), ﴿unless both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾. Hamzah read yakhafa (fear) with a ḍammah on the yā', while the rest read it with a fatḥah. Here "fear" means "suspect" (zann). From this is the saying of the poet:

"News came to me from Nasib, saying what he says,
and I did not fear, in Islam, that you would blame me."

That is, "and I did not suspect."

In ﴿unless both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾ there are four interpretations. The first: that the wife shows rebelliousness and bad character; this is the view of Ibn 'Abbas. (p-295)

The second: that she does not obey him in any command and does not fulfil any oath he takes; this is the view of al-Hasan and al-Sha'bi.

The third: that her tongue shows that she dislikes him; this is the view of 'Ata'.

The fourth: that each of them dislikes the other, so that neither fulfils what Allah has made obligatory upon him regarding the rights of the other; this is the view of Tawus, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and al-Qasim ibn Muhammad. Thabit ibn Yazid narrated from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The khul'at (women who seek khul', divorce by compensation) and the muntaza'at (women who seek removal) are the hypocrites." He meant those who seek khul' from their husbands because they are inclined toward someone else.

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿If you fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah, then there is no blame upon them for what she gives up to be released﴾. There are two views on this. The first: she ransoms herself from him with the dower alone, without any increase; this is the view of 'Ali, 'Ata', al-Zuhri, Ibn al-Musayyib, al-Sha'bi, al-Hakam and al-Hasan.

The second view: it is permissible for her to seek khul' from her husband in exchange for the dower or for more than it; this is the view of 'Umar, Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Nakha'i and al-Shafi'i.

'Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil narrated that al-Rubayyi' bint Mu'awwidh ibn 'Afra' told him: "I had a husband who gave me little bread when he was present, and deprived me when he was absent." She said: "One day I made a mistake, and I said, 'I will seek khul' from you with everything I own.' He said, 'Yes.' So I did it." She said: "My paternal uncle Mu'adh ibn 'Afra' then brought the case to 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, and he permitted the khul', and he ordered that she take what was less than the hair-ornaments of her head."

They differed regarding its abrogation. It is reported from Bakr ibn 'Abdullah that khul' is abrogated by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿But if you wish to replace one wife with another, and you have given one of them a great amount, do not take back anything from it﴾ [al-Nisa': 20]. The majority held that its ruling remains valid, so khul' is permissible.

Ayyub narrated from Kathir, the mawla (freed slave) of Samurah, that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, was brought a rebellious woman. He ordered her to be placed in the house of Kathir, and she was detained there for three days. Then he summoned her and said, "How did you find your place?" She said, "I have not found any ease since I was (married), except these nights in which you detained me." So he said to her husband: "Take khul' from her, even if it be for her earring."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if he divorces her﴾. There are two views on this. The first: it refers to the third divorce; this is the view of al-Suddi.

The second: that this is an option (takhyir) corresponding to His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿or release her with good treatment﴾; this is the view of Mujahid.

﴿then she is not lawful to him after that until she marries another husband﴾, meaning that she is not lawful to the husband who divorced her three times until she marries another husband. On this there are two views. The first: that the marriage of the second husband, if he divorces her, makes her lawful to the first, whether or not he consummated the marriage with her; this is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib.

The second: that she is not lawful to the first husband by the marriage to the second until he consummates it with her, so that she tastes his 'usaylah (sweetness) and he tastes hers, based on the sunnah narrated about it; this is the view of the majority.

On this there are two views. The first: that the marriage of the second husband, if he divorces her, makes her lawful to the first, whether or not he consummated the marriage with her; this is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib.

The second: that she is not lawful to the first husband by the marriage to the second until he consummates it with her, so that she tastes his 'usaylah (sweetness) and he tastes hers, based on the sunnah narrated about it; this is the view of the majority.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 2, verse 231:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when you divorce women and they reach their term﴾ means they came close to the end of their ʿiddah (waiting period), just as a traveller says, "I have reached the town of such-and-such," when he has come near to it.

﴿Then retain them in kindness﴾ means taking them back (rajʿah, revocation of divorce) before the ʿiddah ends, ﴿or release them in kindness﴾ means leaving them alone until the ʿiddah ends.

﴿And do not retain them to harm them, so that you transgress﴾ means that a man takes her back every time he divorces her, until her ʿiddah is prolonged, harming her.

﴿And whoever does that has certainly wronged himself﴾ means, in intending harm; and even if the revocation and the divorce are valid.

Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated from Abu Musa al-Ashʿari: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was angry with the Ashʿaris. They said: One of them says, 'I have divorced, I have taken her back.' This is not the divorce of the Muslims. Divorce the woman before her ʿiddah, and do not take the signs of Allah in jest."

Sulayman ibn Arqam narrated that al-Hasan related to them: "The people in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would divorce or manumit, and it would be said, 'What did you do?' He would say, 'I was joking.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: (Whoever divorces in jest or manumits in jest, it takes effect against him)." Al-Hasan said: "And concerning this was revealed: ﴿And do not take the signs of Allah in jest.﴾"

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 2, verse 232:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when you divorce women and they reach their term﴾. The reaching of the term here means its completion (tanahihi), unlike the reaching of the term in the verse before it, because it is not permitted for her to marry anyone other than him before the end of her waiting period (ʿiddah). Al-Shafiʿi said: "Thus the difference of the two meanings entered upon the separation of the two reachings."

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿do not prevent them﴾. Regarding al-ʿadl (prevention, restraint) there are two views. The first: it is prohibition. From this come their saying: a disease that is ʿuḍāl (incurable), when it refuses to be treated; and so-and-so is ʿuḍlah, meaning a calamity, because he refuses by his cunning.

The second view: al-ʿadl is constriction. From this come their saying: "The plain has constrained (aʿḍala) the army," when it became too narrow for them.

ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab said: "The people of Iraq have constrained me (aʿḍala bī): they are not pleased with any governor, and no governor is pleased with them." And Aws ibn Ḥajar said:

"Your brother who keeps his covenant is not the one who blames you if he turns away, and pleases you when he comes near.
But rather it is the distant one, when you are safe, and your close companion when the matter becomes constrained."

So Almighty and Majestic God forbade the guardians of the woman from constraining her and preventing her from marrying the husbands with whom she is pleased.

As for His saying, Almighty and Majestic: ﴿when they agree among themselves in a fair manner﴾, there are two interpretations. The first: when the two spouses agree. The second: when the woman is pleased with a suitable husband.

Al-Shafiʿi said: "This is clear in the Book of God, the Exalted, indicating that a woman has no right to be married without a guardian (wali)."

The people of interpretation differed regarding who this verse was revealed about, in three opinions: (p-299)

The first: it was revealed concerning Maʿqil ibn Yasar, who married off his sister; then her husband divorced her, and after the waiting period they agreed that he would marry her again, but Maʿqil constrained her. This is the view of al-Ḥasan, Qatadah, and Mujahid.

The second: it was revealed concerning Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah with a paternal cousin of his, whom her husband had divorced; then he proposed to her, but he refused to marry her to him. This is the view of al-Suddi.

The third: it was revealed in general terms, forbidding every guardian from harming his ward among women by constraining her from marriage. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Dahhak, and al-Zuhri.

His saying: ﴿And mothers suckle their children for two full years﴾. Al-ḥawl (الحَوْل) means a year. Regarding its origin there are two views:

The first: it is derived from their saying *ḥāla al-shay'* (حالَ الشَّيْءُ) when a thing turns away from its first state. From this comes *istiḥālat al-kalām* (اسْتِحالَةُ الكَلامِ), meaning speech has turned away from correctness.

The second: it is derived from *al-taḥawwul* (التَّحَوُّلِ) away from a place, which is moving away from it to another place.

He said "two full years" because the Arabs say, "So-and-so stayed in such-and-such a place for two years," when he had in fact stayed a year and part of another, and "he stayed two days," when he had in fact stayed one day and part of another. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And remember Allah during the numbered days. Whoever hastens in two days, there is no sin upon him﴾ [al-Baqarah: 203]. It is known that hastening occurs within one day and part of a day.

The exegetes (*ahl al-tafsīr*, أهْلُ التَّفْسِيرِ, the people of tafsir, i.e., Qur'anic exegesis) differed regarding what this verse indicates concerning suckling for two full years, on two interpretations:

The first: this applies to the woman who gives birth after six months. If she gives birth after nine months, she suckles for twenty-one months, to complete thirty months, based on His saying: ﴿And his carrying and his weaning are thirty months﴾ [al-Aḥqāf: 15]. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās.

The second: this is a command that every child whose parents disagree about his suckling should be suckled for two full years. This is the view of ʿAṭāʾ and al-Thawrī.

Then He said: ﴿And upon the one to whom the child belongs is their provision and their clothing, according to what is customary﴾. By "the one to whom the child belongs" He means the father, who is obligated to provide for the mothers who suckle his child their provision and clothing according to what is customary. Regarding this there are two views:

The first: this applies to a divorced mother who suckles her child; for her is her provision of food and her clothing of garments.

"According to what is customary" means the wage of the equivalent (*ujrat al-mithl*, أُجْرَةُ المِثْلِ). This is the view of al-Ḍaḥḥāk.

The second: it refers to the mother who is still married; for her is her maintenance and clothing according to what is customary for women of her kind, in accordance with the means of the man of wealth and of hardship.

Then He said: ﴿No mother shall be harmed through her child﴾, meaning the mother should not refrain from suckling him in order to harm the father. This is the view of the majority of the exegetes.

ʿIkrima said: it refers to the wet-nurse (*al-ẓi'r*, الظِّئْرُ, the hired nurse) rather than the mother.

Then He said: ﴿Nor shall a father be harmed through his child﴾, and the father is meant by "the one to whom the child belongs," according to the consensus of them all: he should not take the child away from his mother in order to harm her.

Then He said: ﴿And upon the heir is the like of that﴾. Regarding this there are four sayings:

The first: the heir is the child himself. This is the view of Qabīṣa ibn Dhuʾayb.

The second: it is the surviving parent of the child after the death of the other of the two. This is the view of Sufyān.

The third: it is the heir of the child. This is the view of al-Ḥasan and al-Suddī.

The fourth: it is the heir of the child, and regarding this there are four sayings:
- His heir from among his male agnatic relatives (ʿaṣabah, عَصَبَتِهِ) if his father is dead, whether he is a paternal uncle, a brother, a nephew, or a paternal cousin, excluding women among the heirs. This is the view of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and Mujāhid.
- His heirs, men and women alike. This is the view of Qatāda.
- Those among his heirs who are kin by a prohibited degree of relationship (*dhū raḥim muḥarram*, ذا رَحِمٍ مُحَرَّمٍ). This is the view of Abū Ḥanīfa.
- They are the grandfathers, then the mothers. This is the view of al-Shāfiʿī.

Regarding His saying ﴿the like of that﴾ there are two interpretations:

The first: upon the heir is the like of what was upon his father of the wage for his suckling and his maintenance. This is the view of al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, and Ibrāhīm.

The second: upon the heir is the like of that in the prohibition that "no mother shall be harmed through her child." This is the view of al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Zuhrī.

Then He said: ﴿But if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation between them, there is no blame upon them both﴾. *Al-fiṣāl* (الفِصالُ) means *al-fiṣām* (الفِصامُ, separation). It was called *fiṣāl* because the child separates from his mother's breast, from the saying, "So-and-so has separated (*fāṣala*, فاصَلَ) from so-and-so," when he parted from an association that existed between them.

*Al-tashāwur* (التَّشاوُرُ) is the drawing out of an opinion through consultation.

Regarding the time of this weaning by mutual consent there are two views:

The first: that it is before the two years. If both parents agree to wean the child, it is permissible; if one agrees and the other refuses, it is not permissible. This is the view of Mujāhid, Qatāda, al-Zuhrī, and al-Suddī.

The second: that it may be before the two years and after them. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās.

Then He said: ﴿And if you wish to seek wet-nurses for your children﴾, meaning for your children, so He omitted the preposition (*lām*, اللّامَ) because seeking a wet-nurse does not happen for children themselves. This applies when the mother refuses to suckle him, and there is no blame upon him if he seeks another woman as a wet-nurse for him.

﴿When you hand over what you gave, in a customary manner﴾. Regarding this there are three interpretations:

The first: when you, O fathers, hand over to the mothers the wages for what they suckled before they refused. This is the view of Mujāhid and al-Suddī.

The second: when you hand over the children, by the counsel of their mothers, to whomever both parents agree upon to suckle him. This is the view of Qatāda and al-Zuhrī.

The third: when you hand over to the nursing woman who is hired for her wage in a customary manner. This is the view of Sufyān.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 2, verse 234:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days﴾. By "waiting" (tarabbus) is meant the period of ʿiddah (the prescribed waiting period) for a woman whose husband has died. It has been said regarding the addition of the ten days to the four months what Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib and Abu al-ʿAliyah said: that God, exalted is He, breathes the spirit into the fetus during the ten days. Then He mentioned "ten" in the feminine form, giving precedence to the nights over the days when they are combined, because the beginning of the months is the rising of the crescent and the entry of the night. So giving precedence to the first over the second is more appropriate.

They differed regarding whether mourning (ihdad) during this period is obligatory, on two views. One: mourning during it is obligatory; this is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Zuhri. The second: it is not obligatory; this is the view of al-Hasan.

ʿAbdullah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Had narrated from Asma' bint ʿUmays, who said: "When Jaʿfar ibn Abi Talib was killed, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to me: (Mourn for three days, then do what you wish)." Ihdad means abstaining from adornment, perfume, combing the hair, and moving out of the home. (p-303)

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Then when they have reached their term, there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner﴾. If it is asked: what is the meaning of lifting the blame from the men concerning women reaching their term? There are two answers to this. One: the address was directed to the men regarding what the rules of ʿiddah require of the women; so when they reach their term, the blame is lifted from the men in objecting to them and holding them to the rulings of their ʿiddah.

The second: there is no blame upon the men for marrying them after the completion of their ʿiddah.

Then His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿for what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner﴾ has two interpretations. One: (it refers to) perfume, adornment, and moving from a dwelling; this is the view of Abu Jaʿfar al-Tabari. The second: lawful marriage; this is the view of Mujahid.

This verse abrogates His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those of you who die and leave wives behind, let them make a bequest for their wives: provision for a year without eviction﴾ [al-Baqarah: 240]. If it is asked: the latter is earlier, while the abrogating ruling must be later; it is said: in revelation (al-tanzil) it is later, and in recitation (al-tilawah) it is earlier.

If it is asked: why was it placed earlier in recitation though it came later in revelation? It is said: so that the reader reaches its recitation and knowledge of its ruling first; even if he does not recite what follows of the abrogated text, it suffices him.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 2, verse 235:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And there is no blame upon you for what you hint at in the proposal to women﴾. As for ta'ridh (allusion, indirect hinting), it is indicating by speech to something that does not mention marriage (nikah). As for al-khitba with a kasra (khitba, meaning a proposal of marriage), it is seeking marriage. As for al-khutba with a damma (khutba, meaning a sermon), it is speech that includes admonition or delivery of a message.

The permissible ta'ridh during the waiting period (iddah) is that he says to her: "There is no one to stop you from being a woman of good standing, and perhaps Allah will bring you good," or he says: "Many a man desires you," and the like of these expressions.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Or you conceal it within yourselves﴾, meaning what you keep secret of the intention to contract marriage (uqdat al-nikah).

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Allah knows that you will remember them, but do not make promises to them in secret﴾. Regarding "in secret" there are five interpretations. The first: it means fornication (zina), and this is the saying of al-Hasan, Abu Mijlaz, al-Suddi, al-Dahhak and Qatada.

The second: that you do not take from them a covenant and pledges concerning their waiting periods that they will not marry anyone other than you. This is the saying of Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Sha'bi.

The third: that you do not marry them secretly during their waiting periods. This is the saying of Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd.

The fourth: that he says to her: "Do not let yourself escape me." This is the saying of Mujahid.

The fifth: intercourse (jima'), and this is the saying of al-Shafi'i.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Except that you say a proper saying﴾. Its meaning: say a proper saying, and that is the allusion (ta'ridh).

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And do not determine the tie of marriage until the prescribed term reaches its end﴾. In the speech there is an elision, and its estimate is: "And do not resolve upon the tie of marriage," meaning explicit proposal.

Regarding ﴿until the prescribed term reaches its end﴾ there are two sayings. The first: its meaning is "the obligation (fard) of the Writ reaches its term," meaning the end of the waiting period, and the word "obligation" is omitted, being sufficiently indicated by the context.

The second: that by "the Writ" He intended the obligation, as a likeness to a decree (kitab).(p-305)

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 2, verse 236:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿There is no blame upon you if you divorce women as long as you have not touched them﴾. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read: (tumasswahunna) ﴿or until you have specified for them an obligatory payment (faridah)﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions. The first: its meaning is "and you have not specified for them an obligatory payment."

The second: there is an elision in the speech, and its estimated form is: "You have specified or have not specified for them an obligatory payment."

Al-faridah is the dower (sadaq), and it was called faridah because he has made it obligatory for her. The root of al-fard is "the obligatory," as the poet said:

؎ It was an obligation, what you did, just as adultery was an obligation for stoning

And as one says: the ruler "fard" (assigned) a stipend to so-and-so from the fay', meaning he made that obligatory for him.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And provide for them, the affluent according to his means and the straitened according to his means﴾, meaning: give them that by which they may enjoy themselves from your wealth, according to your circumstances in wealth and poverty.

The amount of the provision (mut'ah) has been disputed in three opinions. The first: the mut'ah is a servant, and below that silver (warq), and below that clothing (kiswah); this is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: it is an amount equal to half the dower of her equivalent, and this is the saying of Abu Hanifah.

The third: it is determined by the judgment (ijtihad) of the judge, and this is the saying of al-Shafi'i.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿A provision according to what is reasonable, a duty upon the good-doers﴾. They differed concerning its obligation in four opinions. The first: it is obligatory for every divorced woman; this is the saying of al-Hasan and Abu al-'Aliyah. (p-306)

The second: it is obligatory for every divorced woman except one who has not been consummated with, so for her there is no provision; this is the saying of Ibn 'Umar and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab.

The third: it is obligatory for one who has not been consummated with if no dower has been named for her; this is the saying of al-Shafi'i.

The fourth: it is not obligatory, and the command regarding it is only recommendation (nadb) and guidance (irshad); this is the saying of Shurayh and al-Hakam.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 2, verse 237:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them﴾. This is the first of the two divorces, for one who is averse to a wife before consummation (dukhul), based on the narration of Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not love those who taste (dhawwaqin) [their wives] nor those women who taste [their husbands]." He means separation after tasting (dhawq).

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And you have already specified for them an obligation﴾, meaning a dowry (sadaq), ﴿then half of what you specified﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions. The first: its meaning is that then half of what you specified for them is what is due from you, nothing else is due from you to them, ﴿unless they forgo﴾, meaning the forgoing of the wife, so that her forgoing may be more conducive to her being sought in marriage and may encourage husbands toward her.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿or he in whose hand is the marriage contract should forgo﴾. Concerning this there are three opinions. The first: the one in whose hand is the marriage contract is the guardian (wali), and this is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Tawus, al-Hasan, Ikrimah, and al-Suddi.

The second: it is the husband, and this was said by 'Ali, Shurayh, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Jubayr ibn Mut'im, Mujahid, and Abu Hudhayfah.

The third: it is Abu Bakr, and the master over his slave-woman (al-sayyid fi ummatihi), and this is the view of Malik.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And that you forgo is nearer to righteousness﴾. Concerning the intended addressee of this address there are two opinions. The first: it is addressed to the husband alone, and this is the view of al-Sha'bi. The second: it is addressed to both the husband and the wife, and this is the view of Ibn 'Abbas.

Concerning His saying ﴿nearer to righteousness﴾ there are two interpretations. The first: it is nearer to each of them guarding against wronging the other. The second: it is nearer to guarding against the disobedience of Allah.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 2, verses 238–239:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿Be watchful over the prayers﴾. Regarding guarding them (al-muhafaza), there are two opinions. The first: remembering them (dhikruha).

The second: performing them promptly (ta'jiluha).

Then He, exalted, said: ﴿and the middle prayer﴾. He singled out the middle one for mention even though it is included among the prayers, because of its distinction in merit. Concerning it there are five opinions. The first: it is the afternoon prayer (salat al-asr). This is the view of Ali, Abu Hurayra, Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, Abu Ayyub, Aisha, Umm Salama, Hafsa and Umm Habiba.

Amr ibn Rafi' narrated from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, that Hafsa, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said to the scribe of her copy of the Qur'an: "When you reach the times of the prayers, inform me, until I tell you what I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." When he informed her, she said: "Write: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: Be watchful over the prayers and the middle prayer, and it is the afternoon prayer.'"

Muhammad ibn Sirin narrated from Ubayda al-Salmani, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not pray the afternoon prayer on the day of the Trench (al-Khandaq) until after the sun had set. He said: 'May Allah fill their hearts and their graves with fire! They kept us occupied from the middle prayer until the sun set.'"

al-Taymi narrated from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer."

The second opinion: it is the noon prayer (salat al-zuhr). This is the view of Zayd ibn Thabit and Ibn Umar.

Ibn Umar said: "It is the one in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned toward the qibla."

Ibn al-Zubayr narrated from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray the noon prayer at the time of the midday heat (al-hajira), and he did not pray any prayer that was harder on his companions than it. He said: So the verse was revealed: ﴿Be watchful over the prayers and the middle prayer﴾." And he said: "Before it there are two prayers and after it there are two prayers."

The third opinion: it is the sunset prayer (salat al-maghrib). This is the view of Qabisa ibn Dhu'ayb, because it is neither the fewest nor the most in units, it is not shortened while travelling, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ neither delayed it beyond its time nor hastened it.

The fourth opinion: it is the dawn prayer (salat al-subh). This is the view of Ibn Abbas, Abu Musa al-Ash'ari and Jabir ibn Abdullah. Ibn Abbas said: "It is performed between the blackness of the night and the whiteness of day," relying on His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and stand before Allah in devotion (qanitin)﴾, for qunut is performed in no obligatory prayer except the dawn prayer. Also, it lies between the two night prayers and the two day prayers.

The fifth opinion: it is one of the five prayers, but it is not identified specifically, so that they will be more inclined to guard all of them. This is the view of Nafi', Ibn al-Musayyib and al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym.

There is also a sixth opinion: that the middle prayer is specifically the Friday prayer (salat al-jumu'a).

There is also a seventh opinion: that the middle prayer is congregational prayer (salat al-jama'a) from among all the prayers.

As for naming it "the middle" (al-wusta), there are three aspects. The first: it is the middle of the five prayers in position, since it lies between the two night prayers and the two day prayers.

The second: it is the middle of the prayers in number of units, since the most units in any of them is four and the least is two.

The third: it is the most excellent of the prayers. The middle (wasat) of a thing and its center (wuslata) is its best part, so al-wusta carries the meaning of al-fudla (the most excellent).

Then He, exalted, said: ﴿and stand before Allah in devotion (qanitin)﴾. On this there are six interpretations:

[p-310]

The first: it means obedient (ta'i'in). This is said by Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, al-Sha'bi, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan and Ata'.

The second: silent about what Allah has forbidden you to speak during your prayer. This is the view of Ibn Mas'ud, Zayd ibn Arqam, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd.

The third: humble (khashi'in), a prohibition against playfulness and distraction. This is the view of Mujahid and al-Rabi' ibn Anas.

The fourth: supplicating (da'in). This is narrated from Ibn Abbas.

The fifth: prolonging the standing in prayer. This is the view of Ibn Umar.

The sixth: ..... This too is narrated from Ibn Umar.

There is disagreement about the origin of qunut, on three aspects. The first: its origin is persistence in one matter. The second: its origin is obedience. The third: its origin is supplication.

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿But if you fear, then on foot or riding﴾. Rijal is the plural of rajil (one on foot), and rukban is the plural of rakib (rider), like qa'im and qiyam.

He means: if you fear your enemy, then pray on your feet or on your mounts, standing and walking, facing the qibla or not facing it, gesturing with the head or without gesturing, according to one's capacity.

There is disagreement about the extent of this prayer. The majority hold that it is performed in its full number of units, two rak'as. Al-Hasan said: it is performed as one rak'a when one is in fear.

They also differed on whether one must repeat it after becoming safe. The people of the Hijaz held that the repetition is waived for him because of his excuse.

The people of Iraq held that he must repeat it, because his walking during it is an action that is not part of it.

Then He, exalted, said: ﴿And when you are safe, remember Allah as He taught you what you did not know﴾. On this there are two interpretations. The first: its meaning is, when you are safe, then pray as He taught you. This is the view of Ibn Zayd.

[p-311]

The second: He means, remember Him by praising Him and glorifying Him, as He taught you of the affairs of your religion what you did not know.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 2, verses 238–239:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿Be watchful over the prayers﴾. Regarding guarding them (al-muhafaza), there are two opinions. The first: remembering them (dhikruha).

The second: performing them promptly (ta'jiluha).

Then He, exalted, said: ﴿and the middle prayer﴾. He singled out the middle one for mention even though it is included among the prayers, because of its distinction in merit. Concerning it there are five opinions. The first: it is the afternoon prayer (salat al-asr). This is the view of Ali, Abu Hurayra, Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, Abu Ayyub, Aisha, Umm Salama, Hafsa and Umm Habiba.

Amr ibn Rafi' narrated from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, that Hafsa, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, said to the scribe of her copy of the Qur'an: "When you reach the times of the prayers, inform me, until I tell you what I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." When he informed her, she said: "Write: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: Be watchful over the prayers and the middle prayer, and it is the afternoon prayer.'"

Muhammad ibn Sirin narrated from Ubayda al-Salmani, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not pray the afternoon prayer on the day of the Trench (al-Khandaq) until after the sun had set. He said: 'May Allah fill their hearts and their graves with fire! They kept us occupied from the middle prayer until the sun set.'"

al-Taymi narrated from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer."

The second opinion: it is the noon prayer (salat al-zuhr). This is the view of Zayd ibn Thabit and Ibn Umar.

Ibn Umar said: "It is the one in which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned toward the qibla."

Ibn al-Zubayr narrated from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray the noon prayer at the time of the midday heat (al-hajira), and he did not pray any prayer that was harder on his companions than it. He said: So the verse was revealed: ﴿Be watchful over the prayers and the middle prayer﴾." And he said: "Before it there are two prayers and after it there are two prayers."

The third opinion: it is the sunset prayer (salat al-maghrib). This is the view of Qabisa ibn Dhu'ayb, because it is neither the fewest nor the most in units, it is not shortened while travelling, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ neither delayed it beyond its time nor hastened it.

The fourth opinion: it is the dawn prayer (salat al-subh). This is the view of Ibn Abbas, Abu Musa al-Ash'ari and Jabir ibn Abdullah. Ibn Abbas said: "It is performed between the blackness of the night and the whiteness of day," relying on His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and stand before Allah in devotion (qanitin)﴾, for qunut is performed in no obligatory prayer except the dawn prayer. Also, it lies between the two night prayers and the two day prayers.

The fifth opinion: it is one of the five prayers, but it is not identified specifically, so that they will be more inclined to guard all of them. This is the view of Nafi', Ibn al-Musayyib and al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym.

There is also a sixth opinion: that the middle prayer is specifically the Friday prayer (salat al-jumu'a).

There is also a seventh opinion: that the middle prayer is congregational prayer (salat al-jama'a) from among all the prayers.

As for naming it "the middle" (al-wusta), there are three aspects. The first: it is the middle of the five prayers in position, since it lies between the two night prayers and the two day prayers.

The second: it is the middle of the prayers in number of units, since the most units in any of them is four and the least is two.

The third: it is the most excellent of the prayers. The middle (wasat) of a thing and its center (wuslata) is its best part, so al-wusta carries the meaning of al-fudla (the most excellent).

Then He, exalted, said: ﴿and stand before Allah in devotion (qanitin)﴾. On this there are six interpretations:

[p-310]

The first: it means obedient (ta'i'in). This is said by Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, al-Sha'bi, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan and Ata'.

The second: silent about what Allah has forbidden you to speak during your prayer. This is the view of Ibn Mas'ud, Zayd ibn Arqam, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd.

The third: humble (khashi'in), a prohibition against playfulness and distraction. This is the view of Mujahid and al-Rabi' ibn Anas.

The fourth: supplicating (da'in). This is narrated from Ibn Abbas.

The fifth: prolonging the standing in prayer. This is the view of Ibn Umar.

The sixth: ..... This too is narrated from Ibn Umar.

There is disagreement about the origin of qunut, on three aspects. The first: its origin is persistence in one matter. The second: its origin is obedience. The third: its origin is supplication.

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿But if you fear, then on foot or riding﴾. Rijal is the plural of rajil (one on foot), and rukban is the plural of rakib (rider), like qa'im and qiyam.

He means: if you fear your enemy, then pray on your feet or on your mounts, standing and walking, facing the qibla or not facing it, gesturing with the head or without gesturing, according to one's capacity.

There is disagreement about the extent of this prayer. The majority hold that it is performed in its full number of units, two rak'as. Al-Hasan said: it is performed as one rak'a when one is in fear.

They also differed on whether one must repeat it after becoming safe. The people of the Hijaz held that the repetition is waived for him because of his excuse.

The people of Iraq held that he must repeat it, because his walking during it is an action that is not part of it.

Then He, exalted, said: ﴿And when you are safe, remember Allah as He taught you what you did not know﴾. On this there are two interpretations. The first: its meaning is, when you are safe, then pray as He taught you. This is the view of Ibn Zayd.

[p-311]

The second: He means, remember Him by praising Him and glorifying Him, as He taught you of the affairs of your religion what you did not know.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 2, verses 240–242:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those of you who die and leave wives behind﴾, to the end of the verse.

As for the bequest, it was in place of inheritance, and then it was abrogated (naskh) by the verse of inheritance. As for the "year," the waiting period (iddah) of a widow was a year, and it was abrogated by four months and ten days.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And for divorced women there is provision according to what is reasonable﴾. Regarding this there are three opinions. The first of them: .... The second: that it is for every divorced woman. This is the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr and one of the two opinions of al-Shafi'i.

It is also said that this verse was revealed on a specific occasion, namely that when Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And provide for them, the wealthy according to his means and the poor according to his means, a provision according to what is reasonable, a duty upon the doers of good﴾, a man said: "If I do good, I will do it, and if I do not wish to do so, I will not do it." So Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And for divorced women there is provision according to what is reasonable, a duty upon the God-conscious﴾. This is the view of Ibn Zayd. And the reason He specified the God-conscious (muttaqun) by mention, although the ruling is general, is to honour them.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 2, verse 243–245:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you not considered those who left their homes⁠—⁠﴾, meaning: have you not known?

﴿and they were thousands﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions. The first: they were united in heart (mu'talifi al-qulub), and this is the saying of Ibn Ziyad. The second: they were thousands in number.

Those who hold this view differ about their number, in four sayings. The first: they were four thousand; this was transmitted by Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas. The second: they were eight thousand. The third: they were some thirty-odd thousand, and this is the saying of al-Suddi. The fourth: they were forty thousand, and this is also transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas. The word uluf (thousands) is used for what exceeds ten thousand.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿fleeing from death﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions. The first: they fled from the plague. This is the saying of al-Hasan. Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated, saying: they were four thousand; they went out fleeing from the plague, saying: "We will go to a land where there is no death." So they went out, until, when they were in a certain land, God said to them: "Die," and they died. Then a prophet passed by them and asked his Lord to revive them, and God revived them.

The second opinion: they fled from jihad. This is the saying of 'Ikrimah and al-Dahhak.

﴿So God said to them: "Die"﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions. The first: meaning God caused them to die, just as it is said, "The sky said and it rained," because speech precedes actions, so He expressed the action by it. The second: that He, exalted is He, spoke a word which the angels heard.

﴿Then He revived them﴾. He did this only as a miracle for one of His prophets, whose name was Shom'un (Shemaiah) from among the prophets of the Children of Israel. The period of their death until God revived them was seven days.

Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Juraij said: the smell of death is found in the offspring of that tribe among the Jews until the Day of Resurrection.

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿Who is it that will lend God a goodly loan?﴾ Concerning this there are two interpretations. The first: that it is jihad, and this is the saying of Ibn Zayd. The second: the doors of righteousness, and this is the saying of al-Hasan, and from it is the saying of the poet:

"When you are repaid a loan, repay it; indeed, a young man repays only what is due, not the camel."

Al-Hasan said: The Jews, when this verse was revealed, acted foolishly and said: "God borrows from us, so we are rich and He is poor." So God, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Indeed God has heard the saying of those who said, "Indeed God is poor and we are rich"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 181].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿so that He may multiply it for him many times over﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions. The first: seven hundredfold, and this is the saying of Ibn Zayd. The second: no one knows it except God, and this is the saying of al-Suddi.

﴿And God withholds and extends﴾. Concerning this there are two interpretations. The first: meaning in provision, and this is the saying of al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd. The second: He withholds the charities and extends the reward, and this is the saying of al-Zajjaj.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 2, verse 246:

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Have you not considered the chiefs (al-mala') of the Children of Israel﴾. Al-mala' means the group (al-jama'ah).

﴿After Moses, when they said to a prophet of theirs﴾. The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning him in three opinions. The first: that he was Samuel (Samw'il), and this is the saying of Wahb ibn Munabbih.

The second: Joshua son of Nun (Yushu' ibn Nun), and this is the saying of Qatadah.

The third: Shim'un (Shim'un), whose mother named him so because Allah heard her supplication concerning him, and this is the saying of al-Suddi.

﴿Appoint for us a king, and we will fight in the way of Allah﴾. Concerning the reason for their request there are two sayings. One: that they asked for this to fight the Amalekites, and this is the saying of al-Suddi.

The second: that the tyrants (al-jababirah) who were in their time had subjugated them, so they asked for a king to fight them, and this is the saying of Wahb and al-Rabi'.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 2, verse 247:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And their Prophet said to them, "Indeed, Allah has sent to you Saul as a king."﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and he has not been given abundance of wealth.﴾ Wahb and al-Suddi said: They only denied that he should be king over them, because he was not from the lineage of prophethood nor from the lineage of kingship; rather he was from the most obscure lineage among the Children of Israel. (p-315)

﴿He said, "Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you and increased him broadly in knowledge and physique."﴾ That is, an increase in knowledge and largeness of body.

They differed as to whether this was in him before the kingship. Wahb ibn Munabbih and al-Suddi said: this was in him before the kingship. Ibn Zayd said: the increase in that was after the kingship.

﴿And Allah gives His kingdom to whom He wills, and Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.﴾ Regarding "All-Encompassing" there are three sayings. The first: it means of vast bounty, so the mention of "bounty" is omitted, being sufficiently indicated by the wording, as one says, "So-and-so is great," meaning great in rank.

The second: it means one who widens blessing upon whom He wills of His creation.

The third: it means one who possesses vastness (sa'ah).

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 2, verse 248:

His statement, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And their Prophet said to them: "Indeed, the sign of his kingship⟩ — that is, the sign of his kingship — ﴿is that there will come to you the Ark⟩. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: The size of the Ark was three cubits by two cubits.

﴿In it is tranquility from your Lord⟩. Regarding the tranquility (sakinah), there are six interpretations. The first: it is a gentle, blowing wind that has a face like the face of a human being; this is the view of ʿAlī, peace be upon him. (p-316)

The second: it is a basin of gold from Paradise in which the hearts of the Prophets used to be washed; this is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Suddī.

The third: it is a spirit from God, Exalted, which speaks; this is the view of Wahb ibn Munabbih.

The fourth: it is the signs that are recognized, and they find tranquility in them; this is the view of ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ.

The fifth: it is mercy; this is the view of al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas.

The sixth: it is dignity and gravity; this is the view of Qatādah.

Then He, Exalted, said: ﴿and a remnant of what the family of Mūsā and the family of Hārūn left behind⟩. Regarding it there are four interpretations. The first: the remnant is the staff of Mūsā and the fragments of the tablets; this is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās.

The second: it is the knowledge and the Torah; this is the view of ʿAṭāʾ.

The third: it is jihad in the way of God; this is the view of al-Ḍaḥḥāk.

The fourth: it is the Torah and some of the garments of Mūsā; this is the view of al-Ḥasan.

﴿Carried by the angels⟩. Al-Ḥasan said: The angels carry it between the heavens and the earth, while you see it openly, and they say: Ādam brought down the Ark and the Corner Stone (al-Rukn).

They differed as to where it was before it was returned to them. Ibn ʿAbbās and Wahb said it was in the hands of the Amalekites, who had overpowered the Children of Israel with it. Qatādah said it was in the wilderness of the Wandering (al-Tīh), where Yūshaʿ ibn Nūn had left it. Abū Jaʿfar al-Ṭabarī said: It has reached me that the Ark, the staff of Mūsā, and the Lake of Tiberias, and that these two will come out before the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 2, verse 249:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿When Saul set out with the troops﴾. It is the plural of jund (troop), and ajnad is used for a small number. It was said: they were eighty thousand fighting men.

﴿He said: Indeed, Allah is going to test you with a river﴾. The scholars differed about the river. It is related from Ibn Abbas and al-Rabi' that it is a river between al-Urdunn (Jordan) and Filastin (Palestine). It was also said that it is the river of Filastin. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: the reason for which they were tested with the river was their complaint of the scarcity of water and their fear of thirst.

﴿So whoever drinks from it, he is not of me﴾, that is, he is not of the people of my allegiance.

﴿And whoever does not taste it, he is indeed of me, except one who scoops a handful with his hand﴾. Nafi', Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read (ghurfatan) with a fatha, and the rest read (ghurfatan) with a damma. The difference between them is that ghurfah with a damma is a noun for the water that is drunk, while gharfah with a fatha is a noun for the act.

﴿So they drank from it, except a few of them﴾. 'Ikrimah said: four thousand crossed the river with him, and seventy-six thousand (sic) were hypocrites, and Dawud was among those who were sincere to Allah, Exalted is He.

Ibn Abbas said: whoever drank from it excessively became thirsty, and whoever scooped a handful from it was quenched.

﴿So when he crossed it, he and those who believed with him﴾. It was said: the believers were three hundred and some ten men, the number of the people of Badr.

They differed over whether any disbeliever crossed it with them. It is related from al-Bara', al-Hasan and Qatadah that none crossed it except a believer. Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi said: the disbelievers crossed it, but they withdrew from the believers.

﴿They said: We have no strength today against Jalut and his troops﴾. The scholars differed in the interpretation of that on two views. One: that it was said by those among the believers whose insight was weak. This is the view of al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd.

The second: they are the disbelievers who withdrew. This is the view of Ibn Abbas, al-Suddi,

'Ikrimah said: the four thousand hypocritically withdrew except three hundred and some ten men, the number of the people of Badr, and Dawud was among them.

﴿Those who were certain that they would meet Allah said﴾. These were the remaining believers from among the four thousand.

Regarding "certain" (al-zann) here there are two views. One: it means certainty, and the meaning is those who were certain that they would meet Allah, as Durayd ibn al-Simmah said:

"I said to them: be certain (zunnu) of two thousand armored men, their chiefs in Persian coats of mail, woven."

That is, be certain.

The second: it means those who supposed that they would meet Allah through being killed in the battle.

﴿How many a small company has overcome a large company by the permission of Allah﴾. Fi'ah is a group. ﴿By the permission of Allah﴾. Al-Hasan said: by the help of Allah, because when Allah permits fighting He grants victory in it in the manner in which the permission occurred.

﴿And Allah is with the patient﴾, meaning with victory and support. This is the interpretation of the verse according to the majority of the exegetes.

Some of those who occupy themselves with the subtleties of meanings mentioned that this verse is a parable which Allah struck for the worldly life, likening it to the river: the one who drinks from it is likened to the one who inclines toward it and takes excessively from it, the one who abstains from drinking is likened to the one who turns away from it and renounces it, and the one who scoops from it with his hand is likened to the one who takes from it the measure of his need. The conditions of the three are different in the sight of Allah.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 2, verse 250–252:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So they defeated them by the permission of Allah﴾. Regarding the defeat there are two views. The first: it was not from their own action, and it is ascribed to them only metaphorically (majaz).

The second: when they were forced into it, they became its cause, so it was ascribed to them because of the compulsion.

His saying ﴿by the permission of Allah﴾ may bear two meanings. The first: by Allah's command to them to fight. The second: by Allah's help to them in fighting.

﴿And Dawud killed Jalut (Goliath)﴾. It is related that Jalut came out from the ranks of his army seeking single combat (mubarazah), but no one came out to him. So Talut (Saul) called out in his army: "Whoever kills Jalut, to him is half my kingdom, and I will marry him to my daughter." Dawud came, having taken three stones, and he was short, a shepherd of sheep. Allah had cast into his soul that he would kill Jalut. He said to Talut: "I will kill Jalut." Talut looked down on him when he saw him and said to him: "Have you tested yourself with anything?" He said: "Yes." He said: "With what?" He said: "A wolf fell upon my sheep, so I struck it, then I took its head and cut it off from its body." Talut said: "The wolf is weak. Have you tested yourself against something else?" He said: "Yes. A lion entered my sheep, so I struck it, then I seized it by its jaws and split them. Do you consider this stronger than the lion?" He said: "No." Now Talut had a full coat of mail (dir' sabighah) which would fit only the one who would kill Jalut. So he informed him of it and put it on him, and it fitted. He went to Jalut and struck him with a stone, and it fell between his eyes and came out from the back of his head. It struck a group of his army and killed them, and the people were routed entirely. According to what Ikrimah related, they were ninety thousand.

They differed as to whether Dawud was a prophet at the time he killed Jalut. Some held that he was a prophet, because this act, which is outside custom, could only come from a prophet. Al-Hasan said: he was not a prophet, because it is not permissible for one who is not a prophet to be placed in authority over a prophet.

Ibn al-Sa'ib said: he was only a shepherd, and on this view that would be a preparation for his prophethood afterwards.

Then Talut regretted what he had pledged to Dawud of sharing his kingdom and marrying him to his daughter. They differed as to whether his regret came before the marriage and the sharing or after, on two views. The first: Talut fulfilled his condition, married Dawud to his daughter, mixed him into his rule as himself, then envied him and regretted, and wished to kill him. His daughter learned that he intended to kill her husband, and she was among the most intelligent of women. She set up a skin of wine scented with musk, and at night she placed Dawud's garments upon it. Talut came and said to her: "Where is your husband?" She pointed to the skin, and he struck it with the sword, and the wine gushed out and the scent of musk spread. He said: "May Allah have mercy on you, O Dawud; you were good alive and dead." Then remorse overtook him, and he began to lament over him and weep. When the girl saw her father's grief, she told him the matter. He was delighted, and shared half his kingdom with Dawud. This is the saying of al-Dahhak. On this view, Talut was obedient at his death, through his repentance from his disobedience.

The second view: he regretted before marrying him, concerning his condition and his offer, and he exposed Dawud to death, and said to him: "The daughters of kings must have a dowry befitting their likes, and you are a bold man, so make her dowry the killing of three hundred of our enemies." He hoped by that that he would be killed. Dawud raided and captured three hundred, and Talut found no way but to marry him to her. He married him to her, and his regret increased, so he wished to kill him, and he kept plotting against him until he died. This is the saying of Wahb ibn Munabbih. On this view, Talut died in his disobedience, because he did not repent of his sin.

Makhul related, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has cut off the kinship of kings, so they do not connect with one another out of love for kingship, to the extent that a man among them would kill his father, his son, his brother and his paternal uncle. Except the people of piety, and they are few. And the removal of a mountain from its place is easier than the removal of a kingdom that has not yet come to its end."

﴿And Allah gave him the kingdom and wisdom﴾, meaning Dawud. By kingdom he means authority, and by wisdom prophethood. This was at the death of Talut, after seven years from the killing of Jalut, as related by Ibn al-Sa'ib.

It may bear a second meaning: that the kingdom is the submission of people to his obedience, and the wisdom is justice in his conduct; and this would be after the death of Talut, when he became sole ruler over the affairs of the Children of Israel.

﴿And taught him of what He willed﴾. In this there are two views. The first: the craft of making coats of mail and the measuring in weaving them.

The second: the speech of birds and the wisdom of the Zabur (Psalms).

It may bear a third meaning: that it is the performance of acts of obedience and commanding them, and avoiding sins and forbidding them. Thus on the first view, ﴿of what He willed﴾ refers to Dawud; on the second, ﴿of what He willed﴾ refers to Allah; and on the third, ﴿of what He willed﴾ refers to Allah and what Dawud willed.

﴿And had Allah not repelled some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted﴾. Regarding the repelling there are two views. The first: Allah repels destruction from the land by means of the wicked, as said by Ali, may Allah honour his face. The second: He repels by the fighters from those who sit back, as said by Ibn Abbas.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿the earth would have been corrupted﴾. In this there are two meanings: the first: the people of the earth would have been corrupted. The second: corruption would have spread over the earth.

Regarding this corruption there are two views: the first: disbelief. The second: killing.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 2, verses 253–254:

﴿Those messengers — We preferred some of them over others.﴾ On this there are two views. The first: in the Hereafter, due to their differing in deeds and in bearing burdens.

The second: in this world, by making some of them a khalil (intimate friend of God), some a kalim (one who spoke with God), some a king, subjecting the wind and the devils to some of them, bringing the dead to life through some of them, and healing the blind-born (al-akmah) and the leper (al-abras).

It may also bear a third meaning: in respect of the sharia (revealed law), so that some of them legislated and some did not legislate.

﴿And He raised some of them in rank by degrees.﴾ On this there are two views. The first: that He revealed to some of them in their sleep, and sent angels to some of them while awake.

The second: that He sent some of them to their own people, and sent some of them to all of mankind.

﴿And We gave Jesus, son of Mary, clear proofs.﴾ On this there are two views. The first: the clear arguments and the overpowering demonstrations.

The second: that He created him without a male parent.

﴿And We strengthened him with the Holy Spirit.﴾ On this there are two views. The first: that it refers to Jibril (Gabriel).

The second: that He breathed into him of His Spirit.

﴿And if God had willed, those who came after them would not have fought one another after clear proofs had come to them.﴾ On this there are two views. The first: if God had willed, He would not have commanded fighting after the proof had become clear.

The second: if God had willed, He would have compelled them to faith, and there would not have arisen among them any choice (of belief or disbelief).(p-323)
